correctness_confidence.basis: All analytic proofs across Sections 2-20 were verified by hand and hold as stated, but Equation (28) in Section 21.3 omits a required factor of c in the cluster lower bound, alongside minor notation typos and uninspected external Lean/Colab dependencies.

rigor.basis: Quantifiers, finite periodic domains (2R < n), and local regularity assumptions are stated carefully with explicit counterexamples testing hypothesis boundaries, though marred by the missing factor c in (28) and unupdated cross-references/notation from splicing two drafts.

novelty.basis: The core tools—discrete Fourier modes, rank-nullity, singular Schur complements, Zelazo-Burger cycle cancellation, and the Rumin-Frank spectral density method—are classical; originality lies in specific finite-lattice adapters and diagnostic counterexamples.

significance.basis: Provides useful internal obstructions and observation-rank budgets for flat unit-spacing Hodge forms in the author's programme, but establishes no results for interacting gauge theories, continuum limits, or multiscale covariant renormalization-group operators.

reproducibility.basis: The mathematical text is largely self-contained and verifiable on paper, and commit SHAs/hashes are documented, but no external GitHub sources, Lean 4 proofs, or Colab execution logs could be inspected in this PDF-only review, and internal version metadata is inconsistent.

summary: All 33 pages of ARR-2026-7EPM3V3DP796BBRR-v5.pdf were visually and mathematically inspected in full without external browsing, code execution, or access to the external GitHub repository or Lean/Colab artifacts. The manuscript consolidates two parts: (1) Sections 1-14 establishing necessary observation-dimension and repair-rank budgets for flat unit-spacing lattice Hodge forms under linear and local Fréchet-differentiable observations, regular nonlinear sectors, and directional or full-volume weighted gradient repairs; and (2) Sections 15-24 analyzing sufficient global spectral observations under a critical p = D/2 inverse-moment condition via a finite Rumin-Frank Cwikel bound, sharpness for r < D/2, a log(n) lower bound for dyadic cube-tree partitions, and constructive rectangular-mean bounds. All proofs in Sections 2-20 are mathematically sound. However, a material error occurs in Equation (28) of Section 21.3, where the factor c is omitted from the lower bound on a(x) inside the supplied cubes S_k, invalidating the deduction of the c-coercivity bound (27) on cluster subrectangles for c > 1 and conflicting with the step L^2 <= 8/c in Section 21.4. In addition, splicing the continuation created notation clashes between m and mu, a broken section reference, and uncleaned internal version/tracker notes.
strengths: Exact discrete identities on the finite torus X_n, including the whole-space curl-divergence gradient identity ||GA||^2 = <A, A K_{0,n}> and no-aliasing Fourier band bounds for 2R < n, are proved cleanly without hidden asymptotic assumptions.

The order of quantifiers in the uniform refinement and local tangent obstructions (Theorems 6.1, 7.1, 8.1, 9.1, and 11.2) is handled rigorously, shrinking rays t -> 0 at each fixed lattice size n without requiring uniform implicit-function radii or penalty constants.

Sharp analytic counterexamples justify each structural hypothesis, including C^1 observations failing without quadratic penalty control, C^1 non-quadratic energies and non-surjective constraints in regular sectors, and zero-signed-mean weights with fixed output dimension.

The finite normalized Rumin-Frank spectral density proof of Lemma 17.2 and the variational flow comparison L_a^{-1} <= sum_i T_i^* T_i in Theorem 17.1 are self-contained, handle the zero-frequency kernel explicitly, and give uniform finite-torus constants for all n >= 2.

The compact discrete curl window in Theorem 18.1 and Proposition 19.1 is constructed with exact finite-difference sums (T, V, W) and strictly controlled gradient-start support in [-l, l]^D, cleanly proving both the subcritical inverse-moment refutation and the Omega(log n) dyadic tree depth bound.

The manuscript maintains strict scientific candor regarding scope, explicitly stating that its unit-spacing flat-lattice bounds do not establish an interacting or continuum Yang-Mills mass gap or refute covariant renormalization-group gauge-fixing schemes.
weaknesses: External verification artifacts—including Lean 4 source commits, declaration-map.json, and Colab execution logs referenced in Sections 14 and 22—are not self-contained in the PDF and could not be independently verified.

Sections 15-24 are spliced onto Sections 1-14 as an uncleaned internal dossier, leaving a broken reference to 'Section 1' instead of Section 16 on page 25, conflicting references to internal v5/v6 drafts on pages 20-21, and raw project-tracker shorthand ('PR29 remains 20/41 and TermSource = 0') on page 32.

Notation for the internal Lie-algebra dimension m = N_c^2 - 1 (Sections 2 and 10.1) collides with the mean-weight budget m >= 0 in Section 11, and after switching to mu in Section 15, the text still reverts to m in formulas on pages 25 and 28.

The sufficient spectral theorem (Theorem 17.1) requires a single scalar weight a(x) shared across all derivative directions and field components, which is substantially more restrictive than the componentwise and directional weights treated in Sections 7-11.

The central spatial localization problem—whether critical inverse-moment profiles always admit an O((n/sqrt(1+mu))^D) partition into unrestricted axis-aligned rectangles—remains open, with general threshold partitions achieving only exponent D/4 instead of D/2.

Section 21.3 relies on de Berg's external binary space partition theorem [11] and Section 20.1 relies on the weighted Sobolev inequality of Andres-Deuschel-Slowik [14] as analytic adapters without self-contained proofs in the manuscript.
potential_errors: In Section 21.3, Equation (28) states the inside-cube condition as L_k(L_k-1)/4 <= a(x) <= beta L_k^2 without the factor c, whereas proving c||U||^2 <= E_a(U) + c||C_P U||^2 in (27) via (26) requires c L_k(L_k-1)/4 <= a(x) for x in S_k.

In Section 21.4 (page 30, line 20), the proof that no cube of side L >= 2 can cover 0 writes 'Its lower bound forces L^2 <= 8/c' at a vertex where a(x) = 1, which requires the lower bound in (28) to be c L(L-1)/4 <= a(x) rather than the printed L(L-1)/4 <= a(x).
On page 25, line 2 (proof of Theorem 18.1), the inequality 'mean((mu/a)^r) <= s m^r + 1 <= 2' prints m^r instead of mu^r.
On page 25, line 5 (proof of Theorem 18.1), 'Section 1 forces dim F >= J' is an unupdated cross-reference that should point to Section 16 (page 22) after integrating the appendix into the main text.

On page 28, in Subsection 20.2 (line 7: '||L_a|| <= 8Dm') and Subsection 20.3 (lines 12-13: 'E_mu(u) <= 2Dms' and 's >= cn^D/(2Dm+c)'), the symbol m is erroneously written in place of the scalar weight parameter mu.
In Proposition 11.3 (page 15), the statement writes 'For R > 1', although the formula for A_R(x) and B_{D,R,n} holds for all integers R >= 1 as used in Theorem 11.1.
strong_novelty_candidates: Construction of the all-pairs off-diagonal sum of Zelazo-Burger 4-edge square cancellations on the d-dimensional torus (Section 10.2), giving a nonpositive derivative repair <A, A R_{bar{w}}> <= 0 whose directional positive-part means bar{b}{ij}^+ all grow like n^2.

The concrete separation in Proposition 19.1 showing that for critical inverse-moment profiles on (Z/nZ)^D, any translated full dyadic cube-tree mean observation requires Omega(log n) leaves, whereas an anisotropic rectangular partition succeeds with L^D + D = O(1) blocks.

The constructive counterexample in Section 21.4 trapping a strong vertex 0 between two weak vertices e_1, -e_1 to rule out any universal non-overlapping or overlapping scaled-cube decomposition satisfying (28), while admitting an O(n^D/(1+mu)^{D/2}) grid-plus-singleton rectangular partition.
unresolved_material_objections: In Section 21.3 (page 30), Equation (28) specifies the lower bound on a(x) inside each supplied cube S_k as L_k(L_k-1)/4 <= a(x), omitting the coercivity constant c (unlike the exterior condition a(x) >= c n(n-1)/4). For any c > 1 and L_k >= 2, combining (28) with the rectangle variance bound (26) only yields E{a,R}(U) >= ||U - mean_R U||^2 on cluster fragments R subset S_k, failing to establish the claimed c-coercive inequality (27) highlighted in the Abstract and Section 21.3. Conversely, Section 21.4 explicitly invokes the unprinted factor c when deducing L^2 <= 8/c at a(x) = 1; Equation (28) must be corrected to c L_k(L_k-1)/4 <= a(x) <= beta L_k^2 (or beta rescaled accordingly in the cluster count) for Sections 21.3 and 21.4 to be valid as stated.
